headline: On last trading day, Indian benchmark shares recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: En-masse selling by foreign investors wiped out massive investor wealth.
Rising crude oil prices and global interest rate hikes sparked heavy foreign capital outflows.
Market benchmark indices failed to hold intraday gains amid elevated market volatility.
Persistent selling pressure led to the worst monthly performance since March.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty benchmark indices suffered prolonged declines over recent trading sessions.
SEBI is examining position limits for non-agriculture contracts to boost overall liquidity.
RBI Governor Malhotra reiterated caution regarding cryptocurrencies while supporting underlying technology.
FSSAI reported finding Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener sample unsafe and substandard.
summary: The Indian stock market logged its longest weekly losing streak in 25 years due to relentless foreign fund outflows and global headwinds. Meanwhile, regulatory bodies like SEBI and RBI continue reviewing policies around derivatives and technology. Individual stocks like MTNL, Kotak Bank, and Nestle remained in focus due to specific corporate developments.
